name: Newtonian point-particle mechanics
primitives: Particle positions and velocities, masses, Euclidean space and time.
machinery: Second-order ordinary differential equations; conservation laws when the forces admit the corresponding symmetries.
choices: N, masses, force or potential, and initial conditions. The framework does not select every force law.
closure: Task-ready after those inputs and regularity assumptions are specified.
scope: Particle motion in its classical regime; no quantum or relativistic completion in this variant.
computation: A short law can generate difficult many-body dynamics. Runtime depends on the task, N, accuracy and time horizon.
comparison: A narrower primitive vocabulary than the complete EFMW catalogue; this does not provide a common-scale numerical rank.

name: Classical Maxwell electrodynamics
primitives: Electric and magnetic fields, or an electromagnetic potential modulo gauge, and charge-current sources.
machinery: Linear field equations in vacuum, differential identities, gauge freedom and boundary conditions.
choices: Sources, initial/boundary data and units; material constitutive functions are additional choices if matter is included.
closure: Task-ready for compatible prescribed sources and boundary data; dynamical matter needs its own equations.
computation: Partial differential equations; discretization and geometry control computational cost.
comparison: The EFMW catalogue already includes the Maxwell Lagrangian as ME-012. Reusing it does not create another independent fundamental law.

name: General relativity
variant: Einstein-Hilbert gravity with cosmological constant and specified matter
primitives: A Lorentzian metric, manifold and matter fields.
machinery: Tensor geometry, nonlinear field equations, constraints and diffeomorphism freedom.
choices: G and cosmological constant in a fixed unit convention, matter model, topology and initial/boundary data.
closure: Specified initial-value problems admit a precise formulation; global behavior and singular limits need additional analysis.
scope: Classical gravitation and spacetime; this row does not claim quantum completion.
computation: Gauge fixing, constraints and nonlinear numerical evolution can be demanding despite a compact tensor equation.
comparison: EFMW's gravitational extension inherits this burden and adds a proposed informational source whose independent definition and conservation are open in the frozen review.

name: Minimal Standard Model
variant: Renormalizable three-generation model with massless neutrinos; QCD theta retained
primitives: Gauge fields, chiral quark and lepton fields, and a Higgs doublet with specified representations.
machinery: SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) gauge theory, spinors, symmetry breaking, anomaly cancellation and quantum renormalization.
choices: Conventionally 19 independent physical parameters in this specified variant: 3 gauge, 9 charged-fermion masses, 4 quark-mixing, 2 Higgs and 1 QCD theta. Neutrino masses change the count.
closure: The interaction model is specified; prediction still requires parameter calibration, state preparation and approximation control.
scope: Strong, weak and electromagnetic interactions in this model; gravity and neutrino masses are outside this row.
computation: Perturbative amplitudes and nonperturbative strong-coupling calculations pose different burdens.
comparison: A short Lagrangian hides substantial mathematical structure. EFMW has no correspondingly closed global parameter inventory in the sampled corpus.

name: Operational quantum mechanics
variant: Nonrelativistic Hilbert-space formulation with measurement postulates
primitives: States, operators, an inner product and a specified measurement procedure.
machinery: Schrodinger evolution, spectral probabilities and state-update rules.
choices: Hilbert space, Hamiltonian, preparation, observables and apparatus model.
closure: Calculationally specified for a stated system and measurement; the ontology of the measurement postulates is not fixed by this operational description.
scope: Nonrelativistic quantum predictions, not a proposed unification of gravity.
computation: The state-space size can grow rapidly with subsystem count despite a compact evolution equation.
comparison: A framework for prediction and an ontology are different comparison units; this row is included as a baseline.

name: Bohmian mechanics
variant: Nonrelativistic particle guidance with a wavefunction
primitives: Particle configuration plus wavefunction; interpretation of the wavefunction adds a further ontological choice.
machinery: Schrodinger evolution and a guidance equation; entangled states guide configurations jointly.
choices: Hamiltonian, initial wavefunction and configuration; equilibrium-distribution assumptions connect the theory to ordinary quantum statistics.
closure: The selected dynamical formulation is explicit. Relativistic or field-theoretic versions require separate specification.
scope: An alternative account of nonrelativistic quantum phenomena.
computation: Wavefunction evolution plus trajectories; adding trajectories does not remove many-body wavefunction costs.
comparison: Adds a definite state variable and law to a fixed quantum baseline; its theoretical increment is more readily isolated than the whole EFMW programme.

name: Everett relative-state quantum mechanics
variant: Unitary universal wavefunction with relative records
primitives: Universal quantum state and subsystem-relative records.
machinery: Unitary evolution and the structure of correlations; no additional physical collapse step in this formulation.
choices: Hamiltonian, initial state and the account connecting relative records and probability to experience.
closure: A compact dynamical postulate; the interpretation of probability and records must be included in an ontological comparison.
scope: Quantum foundations; the 1957 formulation does not itself supply a complete quantum-gravity model.
computation: The same large Hilbert spaces can appear as in ordinary quantum mechanics.
comparison: Many described branches do not mean many independent equations. Counting worlds is not a measure of law complexity.

name: GRW spontaneous localization
variant: Nonrelativistic discrete-collapse model; flash-ontology presentation distinguished
primitives: Wavefunction with spontaneous localization; flashes or matter density require an explicit ontology choice.
machinery: Unitary evolution between stochastic localization events; a specified localization law.
choices: Collapse rate and localization width in the usual simple model, in addition to the ordinary Hamiltonian and state choices.
closure: An explicit stochastic process after choosing the variant and its constants; field-theoretic and relativistic extensions are separate models.
scope: Quantum measurement and the microscopic-to-macroscopic transition.
computation: Stochastic wavefunction evolution and sampling; cost depends on representation and particle number.
comparison: More explicit collapse dynamics than the catalogue-level EFMW collapse functional, which still needs physical specification.

name: Perturbative superstring framework
variant: Ten-dimensional perturbative superstring formulations, as described by Schwarz (2000)
primitives: Strings, worldsheet fields and their target-space backgrounds; branes enter relevant sectors.
machinery: Worldsheet quantization, supersymmetry, anomaly constraints, mode spectra, interactions and compactification.
choices: String scale, background and compactification/vacuum data; a count of couplings alone omits major choices.
closure: Explicit perturbative calculations exist for selected backgrounds. This source does not uniquely select the observed low-energy world.
scope: A proposed framework including quantum gravity and gauge/matter sectors.
computation: Conformal/worldsheet methods, spectra and sums over worldsheet topology; background dependence matters.
comparison: Documented machinery is extensive. No shared metric establishes that EFMW is more mathematically complex than this framework.

name: Canonical loop quantum gravity
variant: Connection/holonomy and spin-network formulation in Rovelli (1998)
primitives: Gravitational connection/triad variables and quantum states represented by labeled graphs.
machinery: Holonomy-flux algebra, geometric operators and quantum constraints.
choices: Quantization and dynamical-constraint choices, states and matter coupling; the source discusses competing dynamics.
closure: Kinematics and geometric spectra are developed; the selected historical review identifies dynamics as a major open component.
scope: Nonperturbative quantization of gravitation; not a complete particle-physics fit in this selected source.
computation: Graph representation theory and constraint evaluation; finite truncations do not measure whole-theory complexity.
comparison: Discrete geometric spectra do not make the mathematical apparatus simple, and a graph count cannot be compared with EFMW equation count.

name: Causal set program
variant: Locally finite partial orders and growth models in Sorkin (2003)
primitives: Discrete events with causal ordering and local finiteness.
machinery: Order theory, stochastic growth examples and continuum-approximation questions.
choices: A dynamics or quantum measure, initial structures and a map to continuum observables; the order axioms alone do not choose these.
closure: Specified growth models are executable; the selected source distinguishes them from a completed quantum dynamics.
computation: Sampling and comparing large orders can be difficult even when the primitive definition is short.
comparison: A small ontological vocabulary can leave substantial dynamical choices. This illustrates why sparse primitives do not imply closure.

name: Causal dynamical triangulations
variant: Lorentzian triangulated gravitational path integral in the 2013 account
primitives: Causally organized triangulated geometries as a regulator of a sum over spacetimes.
machinery: Regge action, a constrained ensemble, Wick rotation in the construction, Monte Carlo and continuum limits.
choices: Bare couplings, triangulation/topology conventions, ensemble and scaling limit.
closure: Concrete finite-regulator simulations; a continuum interpretation requires scaling analysis.
scope: Nonperturbative quantum spacetime. Regulator simplices need not be interpreted as final fundamental particles.
computation: Large statistical ensembles and finite-size/continuum extrapolations.
comparison: Implementation size and a set of geometric rules measure different things; neither is comparable to the raw length of the EFMW catalogue.

name: Asymptotic safety gravity
primitives: Metric fields and a scale-dependent effective action.
machinery: Functional renormalization-group equation, gauge fixing, Ward identities and truncation of theory space.
choices: Truncation, regulator and renormalization trajectory; the complete relevant-parameter count is not supplied by one truncation.
closure: A chosen truncated flow is computable. Conclusions about the full theory require controlling truncation dependence.
scope: A possible ultraviolet completion of gravitational field theory.
computation: Coupled flows and functional/operator expansions can grow in complexity as truncations improve.
comparison: One functional equation can encode infinitely many possible operators. Printed-equation count misses this burden.

name: Noncommutative spectral-action model
variant: Chamseddine–Connes–Marcolli 2006/2007 Standard Model plus gravity construction
primitives: A spin manifold and finite noncommutative geometry represented through algebra, Hilbert space and Dirac-operator data.
machinery: Spectral action, geometric constraints and an expansion yielding gravity and particle-physics terms.
choices: Finite algebra/representation, Dirac-operator data, cutoff function/scale and associated couplings.
closure: An explicit effective action for a specified geometric construction. Its historical parameter relations are model predictions, not automatic empirical facts.
scope: An effective unification of the Standard Model with neutrino mixing and gravity.
computation: Spectral geometry, representation theory and effective-action expansion.
comparison: A compact spectral expression packages considerable structure; it supplies a concrete comparator for EFMW's proposed common action.

name: Wolfram hypergraph program
primitives: Relations or hypergraphs and rewrite rules, with causal/multiway structures built from updates.
machinery: Discrete rewriting, causal invariance and proposed links between limiting structures and physical laws.
choices: Rule, seed, updating/multiway treatment and physical-observable map.
closure: A selected rewrite system can be simulated. The framework description does not by itself choose a unique physical model.
scope: A proposed route to fundamental physics from discrete computational structures.
computation: Rule matching and growth of state histories; short rules can produce large calculations.
comparison: Like EFMW, a broad programme must be distinguished from a fully selected physical model. Shared ambition does not establish equivalence.

name: EFMW canonical corpus
variant: 102-entry catalogue plus the explicitly frozen review overlay
primitives: Proposed scalar/informational fields, metric and conventional fields, recursive state/model variables, collapse operators and additional application constructs.
machinery: Mix of tensor/PDE relations, actions, ordinary recurrences, statistical functionals and operational acceptance criteria.
choices: Functions such as F, potentials and coupling/observer maps remain task-dependent or unspecified; no single independent-parameter inventory is established.
closure: Several scoped mathematical models are encoded, but the frozen review explicitly leaves physical identification, a non-circular interpretation and key conservation/analytic obligations unresolved.
scope: Broad physics and cross-domain programme including cognition, monitoring, risk and ethics. Breadth of labels is not demonstrated unification.
computation: Some kernels are inexpensive; coupled continuum models can be expensive. A whole-theory runtime or complexity class is undefined without a fixed problem.
comparison: Best described by a heterogeneous complexity profile and open interfaces. A global complexity rank is not established.
